verdict.rationale: Goodwin's Founders Workbench publishes a financing guide that explains how SAFEs convert at an equity financing and how they differ from convertible notes. Its venture capital practice page states a 180+ lawyer team that handles early-stage venture deals for over 1,200 emerging companies. The evidence shows only a brief explainer excerpt and a general early-stage practice claim, not documented depth on SAFEs or convertible notes for pre-seed and seed rounds. missing for 10: downloadable SAFE or convertible note forms or generators, an explicitly stated pre-seed/seed convertible-instrument practice with deal experience, deeper convertible note explainer content, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, the firm documents deep experience with SAFEs and convertible instruments for pre-seed and seed rounds — published explainers, forms, or a stated early-stage financing practice

citations.quote: The Safe will convert into equity at the time of an equity financing, usually at a discounted rate and/or subject to some maximum value. Unlike a convertible note, the Safe does not accrue interest or have a maturity date.

Goodwin has a team of over 180 lawyers nationwide, experienced in venture capital, who handle early and growth stage venture deals, providing dedicated representation to over 1,200 emerging companies and entrepreneurs
Founders Workbench is a resource to help ease the process by providing you with free information and tools
